text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn will no longer have to field questions from MPs if a Socialist proposal to abolish Prime Minster's question time is approved by the House on Tuesday.
- Opposition MPs attacked the government for failing to provide compensation for energy price rises which take effect Tuesday.

- Hungary's inflation rate and public finance deficit are declining for the first time while the external economic balance is not deteriorating, National Bank president Gyorgy Suranyi declared on Monday
- Two commercial channels can begin broadcasting on September 1 following Monday's announcement that consortia MTM-SBS and Magyar RTL have won the tenders for the two channels.
- Hungary is to bid for a Central European High Altitude Traffic Routing Centre (Ceats) to coordinate air traffic above 9,000 metres.
- Postabank intends to call down the first instalment of a 12-billion-forint state gurantee covering the bad bank's debts, according to a letter the bank sent to the Finance Ministry.
- Judges investigating public office holders' connections with the communist-era secret services will in the next few days consider evidence of Prime Minister Gyula Horn's past involvement.
